tip: Some verbs shift e to i in the er form: vergessen becomes er vergisst, while the infinitive keeps the e.
Passive is a form of werden plus a past participle. Past passive uses wurde: Das Problem wurde gelöst = it was solved.
werden plus an infinitive builds the future: wir werden uns treffen = we will meet. The infinitive treffen goes to the end.
German often uses the present for the future when a time word is given: wir sehen uns nächste Woche means we will see each other next week.
With two objects the person is dative and the thing is accusative: seinem Chef comes before eine Nachricht.
aufhören is a separable verb, so in a command the prefix splits off and follows the verb: Hör auf = stop.
For days and weekends German uses am, short for an dem: am Wochenende = on the weekend, am Montag = on Monday.
es zieht is a fixed phrase meaning there is a draft. The es is a dummy subject with no real thing behind it.
The ihr command is just the ihr verb form without the pronoun: ihr esst becomes Esst, ihr genießt becomes genießt.
über takes the accusative when there is movement across: über den gefrorenen Teich shows motion, so den, not dem.
The polite command puts the verb first, then Sie: Lesen Sie bitte. The pronoun Sie stays, unlike in the du or ihr command.
bevor sends its verb to the very end of the clause: bevor ich hinausgehe, not bevor ich gehe hinaus.
außerhalb takes the genitive: Außerhalb der Geschäftszeiten = outside business hours. That is why it is der, not die.
Comparatives add -er and use als for than: teuer becomes teurer, dropping the second e. teurer als = more expensive than.
When a time phrase opens the sentence, the verb stays second and the subject follows: Gestern Abend beobachtete der Astronom.
Verbs of motion form the perfect with sein, not haben: wir sind gereist = we traveled. The participle gereist goes last.
A modal like können pushes the main verb to the end as an infinitive: wir können nicht anfangen = we cannot start.
wegen takes the genitive: Wegen des Streiks = because of the strike. That genitive is why it reads des Streiks, not der Streik.
sein has an irregular ihr command: Seid, not Seit. Seid pünktlich = be on time, said to several people.
Patient is an n-noun: it adds -n in every case except the nominative, so dem Patienten, not dem Patient.
Passive under a modal is a participle plus werden: muss repariert werden = must be repaired. werden stays in its base form.
um plus zu plus a verb expresses purpose: Um besser Deutsch zu lernen = in order to learn German better.
